info.title: Power Automate API
info.description:
The Power Automate service API (`api.flow.microsoft.com`), which addresses flows under the `Microsoft.ProcessSimple` resource provider -- the internal name Power Automate still carries on the wire.

It is a sibling of the Power Apps API rather than part of the Power Platform API: same shape, same `/providers/{rp}/environments/{env}/...` convention, same `scopes/admin` elevation, and its own host.

Unofficial and reverse-engineered. Every operation here was read from a working third-party client's call sites rather than from documentation, so the routes and methods are real and the response bodies are deliberately unmodelled -- see the [README](https://github.com/AdamCoulterOz/powerplatform-apis/tree/main/flow).

x-notes.note:
**This spec is client-derived and nothing in it has been observed on the wire.** It exists because the corpus was silent on Power Automate while every other Power Platform surface was covered, and a reader comparing a working client against the corpus would have found nothing at all here.

That makes it the weakest spec in the corpus by evidence: no operation carries `x-probe-verified`, no response body is modelled, and the api-version is the one shipped clients send rather than one the service was seen to accept. Treat it as a map of what exists and is called, not as a contract.

servers.description: The global Power Automate host. Regional prefixes such as `europe.` and `emea.` are used by some clients; none has been verified here.

get.description: Environments visible to the caller on the Power Automate host. Distinct from the BAPI and Power Platform API environment lists: this one reports what the flow service knows, which can lag the platform.

parameters.name: api-version
parameters.description: The API version. Shipped clients send `2016-11-01`; the admin flow list uses a `/v2/` path segment instead of a newer version.
